prose.hook: Straddling the Equator on Central Africa's Atlantic coast, this country packs most of its people into a narrow corridor: about 70% live in Brazzaville, Pointe-Noire, or along the railroad connecting them. Beneath its coastal plains and plateaus lie petroleum, gold, copper, potash, and uranium, and crude oil dominates what the country sells to the world.
prose.physicalGeography: The terrain runs from a coastal plain along the South Atlantic inland through a southern basin, a central plateau, and a northern basin. The country sits between Angola and Gabon in Central Africa, with the ocean forming its western edge.
prose.climate: Lying astride the Equator, the country experiences a tropical climate marked by persistent high temperatures and humidity that make conditions particularly enervating. A rainy season runs from March to June, followed by a dry season from June to October, and seasonal flooding occurs.
prose.economy: The economy runs primarily on oil and natural resources, and recovery from the mid-2010s oil price collapse has been slow, worsened further by COVID-19. Extreme poverty is increasing, especially in southern rural regions, and the country faces a growing likelihood of debt default while attempting to implement CEMAC-recommended reforms. Industries include petroleum extraction, cement, lumber, brewing, sugar, palm oil, soap, flour, and cigarettes, with crude petroleum, refined copper, gold, and wood among the main exports.
prose.peopleAndCulture: The Kongo (Bakongo) form the largest ethnic group at 40.5%, followed by the Teke and Mbochi, alongside smaller communities including the Sangha, Punu, and Pygmy peoples, plus a notable foreigner population. Religiously, Roman Catholics make up the largest share at 33.1%, followed by Awakening Churches/Christian Revival adherents and Protestants, with smaller numbers of Muslims, Kimbanguists, and those professing no religion.
